sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: In July 1798, an English poet visited the countryside on the banks of the River Wye.
sentences.zh: 1798年7月，一位英国诗人造访了怀河畔的乡村。

sentences.en: On seeing the natural beauty of the area, William Wordsworth composed a poem.
sentences.zh: 在目睹了当地的自然美景后，威廉·华兹华斯创作了一首诗。

sentences.en: It's titled, Lines Written a Few Miles Above Tintern Abbey.
sentences.zh: 诗的标题是《丁登寺上方几英里处所作的诗行》。

sentences.en: At one point, he describes the effect of the landscape on his psychological state.
sentences.zh: 在诗中，他描述了这种景观对他的心理状态产生的影响。

sentences.en: But more than two centuries after Wordsworth composed his poem, some scientists today are asking an unusual question.
sentences.zh: 但在华兹华斯创作这首诗两百多年后的今天，一些科学家提出了一个不同寻常的问题。

sentences.en: Were the romantics on to something?
sentences.zh: 浪漫主义者们是否发现了什么真谛？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we look at what happens when we stop, really stop, to smell the roses.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将探讨当我们停下脚步，真正停下来去“闻闻玫瑰花香”时，会发生什么。

sentences.en: For centuries, one of the central challenges in human behavior has been the problem of suffering.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，人类行为的核心挑战之一就是苦难问题。

sentences.en: We all have aches and ailments, setbacks at work, and conflicts in personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们都有病痛和烦恼，工作上的挫折，以及人际关系中的冲突。

sentences.en: Many years ago, the psychologist Dakar Keltner found himself in a world of suffering.
sentences.zh: 多年前，心理学家达克·凯尔特纳发现自己陷入了苦难之中。

sentences.en: He was in his early 30s and had just moved from California to Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 那时他刚过30岁，刚从加利福尼亚搬到威斯康星州。

sentences.en: What happened to me, Shankar, is I lived a life largely in California, in the hills, in the mountains, in the oceans, in the culture, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，当时发生的情况是，我之前的生活主要是在加州度过的，那里有山丘、山脉、海洋、文化等等。

sentences.en: And I went 2,000 miles away, and it was flat.
sentences.zh: 然后我搬到了2000英里外的地方，那里地势平坦。

sentences.en: And there were storms, and there was snow, and people rooted for the Packers, and they ate bratwurst, and there was no Mexican food, and the weather, and the cold.
sentences.zh: 那里有暴风雨，有积雪，人们支持包装工队，吃着德国香肠，没有墨西哥食物，还有那里的天气，那里的寒冷。

sentences.en: I felt like Camus' stranger in a way, like, I am in a strange land that I just physically, temperature-wise, climate-wise, people-wise, I felt like a fish out of water,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我感觉自己就像加缪笔下的那个异乡人，身处一个陌生的国度，无论是从生理上、气温上、气候上，还是人际关系上，我都觉得自己像条离水的鱼，

sentences.en: even though I look like somebody from Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 尽管我看起来就像个威斯康星本地人。

sentences.en: I'm, you know, of Northern European heritage.
Dakar, who was just starting his career as a professor, started to experience extreme bouts of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 当时刚开始教授生涯的达克，开始经历极度的焦虑发作。

sentences.en: I come from a family on my mom's side that has a lot of anxiety, and I started to have profound panic attacks,
sentences.zh: 我母亲那边的家族有很严重的焦虑症史，我开始出现严重的恐慌发作，

sentences.en: really beginning with the day that I departed to drive across the country to Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 真正开始于我开车横跨全国前往威斯康星的那一天。

sentences.en: I had probably, I would say, 70 or 80 a year, really technicolor, full-blown panic attacks.
sentences.zh: 我一年大概会有70到80次，那种非常生动、全面的恐慌发作。

sentences.en: When I was teaching, when I would go see a movie to try to relax, when I would fly on an airplane to go to a conference, when I would hear from a colleague,
sentences.zh: 当我教学时，当我去看电影试图放松时，当我坐飞机去参加会议时，当我收到同事的消息时，

sentences.en: and it really caught me off guard, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我措手不及，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Like, wow, why am I feeling so estranged and anxious all the time?
sentences.zh: 就像是，哇，为什么我一直感到如此疏离和焦虑？

sentences.en: Everything around Dakar seemed to remind him of his isolation.
sentences.zh: 达克周围的一切似乎都在提醒他的孤独。

sentences.en: Everywhere he went, he experienced vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 无论他走到哪里，他都感到脆弱。

sentences.en: He felt that his life was about to end.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己的生命即将走到尽头。

sentences.en: My God, you know, for those people out in the audience who've had real panic attacks, they are spectacular, and they hit you, and you literally, the brain says you're dying,
sentences.zh: 天哪，你知道，对于那些在听众席中经历过真正恐慌发作的人来说，那种感觉非常剧烈，它会突然袭击你，你的大脑会真真切切地告诉你，你要死了，

sentences.en: and your body is telling you, you, Dakar Keltner, are dying, and you're about to die right here.
sentences.zh: 你的身体在告诉你，你，达克·凯尔特纳，正在死去，你马上就要死在这里了。

sentences.en: And I remember there was this book about weird stories from Wisconsin about how anxious people ended up dying in Wisconsin,
sentences.zh: 我记得当时有一本关于威斯康星怪谈的书，讲的是那些焦虑的人最终是如何在威斯康星死去的，

sentences.en: because they would go out and start tilling the earth on their farm at two in the morning, you know, and everything was frozen, and the guy froze to death.
sentences.zh: 因为他们会在凌晨两点跑出去开始耕种农场，你知道，当时一切都结冰了，然后那个人就冻死了。

sentences.en: And I was like, this is going to happen to me.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，这也会发生在我身上。

sentences.en: And it was happening to me.
Dakar had moved across the country to join the University of Wisconsin, but his work provided no solace.
sentences.zh: 达克搬到全国另一端加入威斯康星大学，但他的工作并没有给他带来慰藉。

sentences.en: I was getting rejected for grants.
sentences.zh: 我的研究经费申请被拒绝了。

sentences.en: There was a conference on the social nature of emotion, which is what I was writing about and defined my career on.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个关于情感社会本质的会议，这正是我所写的内容，也是我职业生涯的定义所在。

sentences.en: I started to dream about people broadcasting all the rejections of my papers and ideas and the like.
sentences.zh: 我开始梦见人们在广播我所有被拒的论文和想法等等。

sentences.en: You know, I got a very mediocre to bad mid-career review.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我得到了一份非常平庸甚至糟糕的中期职业评估。

sentences.en: It was a real struggle, to be quite honest, and a lot of suffering.
sentences.zh: 说实话，那真是一场挣扎，充满了苦难。

sentences.en: So like many of us who have been through something similar, you try to do a number of things to make yourself feel better.
sentences.zh: 所以，像许多经历过类似事情的人一样，你会尝试做很多事情来让自己感觉好一点。

sentences.en: At one point, you and some fellow academics banded together to form a basketball team.
sentences.zh: 有一次，你和一些学术界的同仁组建了一支篮球队。

sentences.en: Why did you do that, and how did it go?
sentences.zh: 你为什么那么做，结果如何？

sentences.en: Well, we formed this team that we named the Laughing Amygdala.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们组建了一支球队，取名为“大笑的杏仁核”。

sentences.en: Because the Amygdala was all the rage at the time.
sentences.zh: 因为当时“杏仁核”非常流行。

sentences.en: It was Joe Ledoux, the Amygdala, the Threat Center, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 那是乔·勒杜克斯的杏仁核，威胁中心等等。

sentences.en: And what was great about our team, Shankar, is we were all professors and three graduate students.
sentences.zh: 我们球队最棒的地方在于，尚卡尔，我们都是教授，还有三名研究生。

sentences.en: And we had this really unlikely team, and we won championships on the campus.
sentences.zh: 我们组成了一支非常不可思议的球队，还在校园里赢得了冠军。

sentences.en: We beat the football team, you know, the fraternities, and people were just stunned, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们打败了橄榄球队，你知道，还有那些兄弟会，人们都惊呆了。

sentences.en: And so it was this magical run.
sentences.zh: 那真是一段神奇的经历。

sentences.en: And, you know, Shankar, from the solitary life of 3 a.m., I would go to the gym and play.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，尚卡尔，从凌晨三点的孤独生活中，我会去体育馆打球。

sentences.en: And basketball is five people flowing in motion in a sense of, you know, just we're all connected doing things together.
sentences.zh: 篮球是五个人在流动中配合，那种感觉就是，我们连接在一起，共同完成某事。

sentences.en: And when I'd walk to the gym, it felt like a sanctuary, that I would go there and leave behind the anxiety.
sentences.zh: 当我走向体育馆时，它感觉就像一个避难所，我去那里，把焦虑抛在脑后。

sentences.en: I want to play a clip of music here, Dakar.
It's from Raw Power, the 1973 album by Iggy Pop and the Stooges.
sentences.zh: 这是伊基·波普和丑角乐队1973年的专辑《Raw Power》中的曲目。

sentences.en: Dakar, what memories does this music hold for you?
sentences.zh: 达克，这段音乐对你来说有什么回忆？

sentences.en: Shankar, one of the, I think one of the deepest mysteries in science right now, in the social sciences, is why does music speak to us?
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我认为目前科学界，尤其是社会科学界最深奥的谜团之一，就是为什么音乐能触动我们？

sentences.en: And why does it speak to our soul?
sentences.zh: 为什么它能触动我们的灵魂？

sentences.en: And when I was in Madison, Wisconsin, I was really, you know, fighting and with anxiety and, you know, trying to find my way in life.
sentences.zh: 当我在威斯康星州麦迪逊市时，我真的在与焦虑作斗争，试图在生活中找到方向。

sentences.en: And at that time, I'd probably seen Iggy Pop, kind of a godfather of punk rock, about six to eight times.
sentences.zh: 那时，我大概看过六到八次伊基·波普的演出，他算是朋克摇滚的教父。

sentences.en: And he played, I think it was in Milwaukee, and I took some friends to the show.
sentences.zh: 他在密尔沃基演出，我带了一些朋友去看。

sentences.en: And it was just like basketball.
sentences.zh: 那感觉就像打篮球一样。

sentences.en: Like, I was leaving behind the heat of anxiety of my academic life, my young career.
sentences.zh: 就像我正在抛开学术生活和年轻职业生涯中焦虑的热浪。

sentences.en: And I go to the show, and I get up close, and we're in this throbbing mosh pit that scientists now study.
sentences.zh: 我去现场，挤到前面，置身于科学家们现在研究的那种躁动的“冲撞区”里。

sentences.en: And he comes out, and he sings all his great songs, you know, Raw Power, and, you know, Lust for Life, and Passenger.
sentences.zh: 他走出来，唱着他所有伟大的歌曲，你知道，《Raw Power》，还有《Lust for Life》和《Passenger》。
我熟悉这些歌，我跟着唱。

sentences.en: You know, at one point, he dives out into the crowd, and I'm right there, and I hold him, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一次，他跳入人群，我就在那里，我托住了他。

sentences.en: And he's aloft on all of our hands.
sentences.zh: 他被我们所有人的手托举着。

sentences.en: And Shankar, I touch his skin, and his skin feels like God.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我触碰了他的皮肤，他的皮肤感觉就像神一样。

sentences.en: You know, I'm just like, I can't believe I'm holding Iggy Pop's bicep.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时想，我简直不敢相信我正托着伊基·波普的二头肌。

sentences.en: So, when I leave an Iggy Pop show, I'm drenched in sweat.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我离开伊基·波普的演唱会时，我浑身湿透。

sentences.en: I don't know who I am.
And I feel alive and pure.
So, I go back to Wisconsin, and I look at his CD, and it says,
sentences.zh: 于是，我回到威斯康星，看着他的CD，上面写着：

sentences.en: If you feel like writing me, drop me a line.
sentences.zh: 如果你想写信给我，给我写几行字。

sentences.en: You know, and I tell him about all my stories, you know, seeing him and how important he's been to me as a young professor, handling my struggles.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我告诉了他我所有的故事，看他的演出，以及作为一名年轻教授，他在我应对挣扎时对我有多重要。

sentences.en: Six months later, I get a letter back in this little shaky scrawl.
sentences.zh: 六个月后，我收到了一封回信，字迹有些颤抖。

sentences.en: And it's like, he says, Thanks for all of your stories.
sentences.zh: 他说，谢谢你所有的故事。

sentences.en: Good luck getting access to the young skulls at UW.
sentences.zh: 祝你在威斯康星大学吸引那些年轻的头脑时好运。

sentences.en: And I like, I'm getting goosebumps talking about this now.
sentences.zh: 现在谈起这个，我还会起鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: Like, I held the letter, and I'm like, my life's okay.
sentences.zh: 我拿着那封信，心想，我的生活没问题。

sentences.en: And when I'd bounce up on the stage and teach my 300 students, getting my mediocre reviews and making mistakes here and there, I felt more strong and alive.
sentences.zh: 当我跳上讲台给300名学生上课，得到平庸的评价，偶尔犯错时，我感到更加强大和充满活力。

sentences.en: You were touched by the hand of God here, Dakar.
sentences.zh: 你在这里受到了上帝之手的触碰，达克。

sentences.en: Another time, Dakar, you and your wife were outside watching a summer storm approach.
sentences.zh: 还有一次，达克，你和你的妻子在外面看着一场夏日风暴逼近。
当时龙卷风警报正在响起。

sentences.en: Describe for me what was happening, and tell me what you both did next.
sentences.zh: 描述一下当时发生了什么，并告诉我你们接下来做了什么。

sentences.en: My wife, Molly, grew up in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我的妻子莫莉在旧金山长大。

sentences.en: You know, we both were adapting to the weather and the climate and the landscape.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都在适应那里的天气、气候和景观。

sentences.en: And this storm starts rolling in, and you could see it from afar.
sentences.zh: 风暴开始卷来，你可以从远处看到它。

sentences.en: And they looked strong and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来既强大又危险。

sentences.en: And then there was some kind of warning that said, get into your basement, a tornado warning.
sentences.zh: 然后出现了一些警报，说进入地下室，是龙卷风警报。

sentences.en: And I think tornadoes did land that day.
sentences.zh: 我想那天确实有龙卷风着陆了。

sentences.en: And for whatever reason, we said, let's feel it.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，我们说，去感受一下吧。

sentences.en: Let's get out in the storm.
Let's see what the mystery is.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看其中的奥秘是什么。

sentences.en: And let's just, you know, we couldn't really explain it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的无法解释原因。

sentences.en: But we sat out on our swing, on our front porch, as this wild storm ripped through, you know, Madison for half an hour or whatever it was.
sentences.zh: 但我们坐在前廊的秋千上，看着这场狂暴的风暴席卷麦迪逊，持续了半小时还是多久。

sentences.en: And rain and lightning and massive winds.
And again, it felt, I just felt so alive and free of the shackles of my anxiety at the time.
sentences.zh: 再一次，我感到自己如此鲜活，摆脱了当时焦虑的枷锁。

sentences.en: So it was a striking experience.
sentences.zh: 那真是一次震撼的经历。

sentences.en: So these all seem like very different experiences, enjoying teamwork in a basketball game, being part of a crowd at a music concert, watching a storm approach.
sentences.zh: 这些看起来都是非常不同的经历，享受篮球比赛中的团队合作，在音乐会上成为人群的一部分，观看风暴逼近。

sentences.en: Is there a common thread that connects these experiences, Dakar?
sentences.zh: 达克，这些经历之间有什么共同点吗？

sentences.en: You know, it was really interesting, Shankar, because I was really struggling in these four years.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的很有趣，尚卡尔，因为在那四年里我真的挣扎得很厉害。

sentences.en: And I, you know, I was chronically anxious, tons of panic attacks, struggling career-wise, really feeling away from home.
sentences.zh: 我长期焦虑，频繁恐慌发作，事业受挫，真的感觉远离家乡。

sentences.en: And I didn't know how to find happiness, which has been a life's puzzle for me in many ways.
sentences.zh: 我不知道如何找到幸福，这在很多方面一直是我人生的难题。

sentences.en: And I think what I was doing in these experiences is I was getting outside of myself on the basketball court.
sentences.zh: 我认为我在这些经历中所做的是，我在篮球场上走出了自我。

sentences.en: It's just the motion and the physicality and you're playing with five people.
sentences.zh: 那只是运动和身体的参与，你和五个人一起打球。

sentences.en: And I lost myself right up front, like in a mosh pit near seeing Iggy Pop and feeling the music.
sentences.zh: 我在看伊基·波普演出时的冲撞区里迷失了自我，感受着音乐。

sentences.en: And I lost myself in the storm.
sentences.zh: 我在风暴中迷失了自我。

sentences.en: You know, I was just like, I was throwing myself into things where I could lose myself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我只是把自己投入到那些能让我迷失自我的事情中。

sentences.en: Like William Wordsworth two centuries ago, Dakar had begun to discover ways out of his narrow preoccupations.
sentences.zh: 就像两个世纪前的威廉·华兹华斯一样，达克开始找到摆脱狭隘心境的方法。

sentences.en: When we come back, the connections between these different experiences and the science behind a mind-expanding emotion.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨这些不同经历之间的联系，以及一种能拓展思维的情绪背后的科学。
你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: University of California Berkeley psychologist Dakar Keltner studies what he calls pro-social emotions,
sentences.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的心理学家达克·凯尔特纳研究他所谓的“亲社会情绪”，

sentences.en: feelings like love, compassion, and gratitude.
Earlier in his life, he tried to get himself through a difficult time by immersing himself in sports, in music, and in the beauties of the natural world.
sentences.zh: 早年间，他试图通过沉浸在体育、音乐和自然世界的美景中来度过一段艰难时期。

sentences.en: In time, he realized there was a common connection between these activities.
sentences.zh: 久而久之，他意识到这些活动之间存在着共同的联系。

sentences.en: They all activated a feeling of being awestruck.
sentences.zh: 它们都激活了一种敬畏感。

sentences.en: Now at the University of California, Berkeley, Dakar has spent years studying the science of awe.
sentences.zh: 现在在加州大学伯克利分校，达克花了多年时间研究敬畏的科学。

sentences.en: Dakar, I want to talk about your scientific explorations of awe.
sentences.zh: 达克，我想谈谈你对敬畏的科学探索。

sentences.en: But so much of your intellectual journey starts with your personal journey.
sentences.zh: 但你的许多智力之旅都始于你的个人旅程。

sentences.en: Both your parents were attuned to the world of art.
sentences.zh: 你的父母都对艺术世界很敏感。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about them?
I really lived a life that really is, in some sense, from my first moments of being born in Mexico, a life as an experiment in awe.
sentences.zh: 从我在墨西哥出生的那一刻起，我所过的生活在某种意义上就是一场关于敬畏的实验。

sentences.en: Now, formative years in Laurel Canyon, California, in the late 60s, so much music going on, Joni Mitchell, The Doors.
sentences.zh: 我在60年代末的加州劳雷尔峡谷度过了成长岁月，那里音乐盛行，琼尼·米歇尔、大门乐队。

sentences.en: My dad was a painter, and he loved awe-inspiring, horrifying work.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是一位画家，他热爱那些令人敬畏、令人恐惧的作品。

sentences.en: Goya, Velasquez, Francis Bacon, and others, right?
sentences.zh: 戈雅、委拉斯开兹、弗朗西斯·培根等等，对吧？

sentences.en: Just as a kid, I was just seeing images all the time.
sentences.zh: 小时候，我一直在看这些图像。

sentences.en: And then my mom loved awe in literature, and was getting her Ph.D., eventually taught at Cal State Sacramento, and loved, you know,
sentences.zh: 我母亲热爱文学中的敬畏感，她在攻读博士学位，后来在加州州立大学萨克拉门托分校任教，她热爱，你知道，

sentences.en: Virginia Woolf and her awesome portrayals of the mind and the romanticism and Wordsworth and Blake.
sentences.zh: 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫，她对心灵、浪漫主义、华兹华斯和布莱克的精彩描绘。

sentences.en: And I would hear quotes of Blake, and she told me about the prelude of Wordsworth, and, you know, and then also D.H.
sentences.zh: 我会听到布莱克的诗句，她会给我讲华兹华斯的《序曲》，还有，你知道，还有D.H.
劳伦斯以及其他人的作品。

sentences.en: And so my parents were pointing me at an early age from, like, five and six, like, here are quotes about awe.
sentences.zh: 所以我的父母在我很小的时候，大概五六岁时，就开始引导我，比如，这些是关于敬畏的诗句。
这些是关于敬畏的画作。

sentences.en: You know, I remember listening to Sgt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得披头士乐队的《佩珀中士》刚发行时，

sentences.en: Pepper's when it came out, The Beatles, together as a family.

sentences.zh: 就像是，生活就是关于敬畏的。

sentences.en: I understand that your family moved to a rural community in the foothills of the Sierras, and you and your brother, Rolf, spent many days roaming outside in nature.
sentences.zh: 我了解到你们一家搬到了内华达山脉山脚下的一个乡村社区，你和你的兄弟罗尔夫花了很多时间在户外大自然中漫游。

sentences.en: My parents, you know, it was 1970.
sentences.zh: 我的父母，你知道，那是1970年。

sentences.en: My mom had just gotten this job at Cal State Sacramento as an English professor, teaching romanticism and the like.
sentences.zh: 我母亲刚在加州州立大学萨克拉门托分校找到一份英语教授的工作，教授浪漫主义文学之类的课程。

sentences.en: And they did what a lot of people did in that era, is they moved to the country where it was cheaper, and we got an old, beat-up Victorian, five acres,
sentences.zh: 他们做了那个时代很多人都会做的事，搬到了更便宜的乡村，我们住进了一栋破旧的维多利亚式房子，有五英亩地，

sentences.en: and there were streams and creeks and ponds and railroad tracks we could follow, you know.
sentences.zh: 那里有溪流、小河、池塘和我们可以沿着走的铁轨，你知道。

sentences.en: And we just wandered after school.
sentences.zh: 放学后我们就四处游荡。
我们不做任何家庭作业。

sentences.en: And then as we got older, what we started to do, Shankar, is go to the rivers, you know, rafting, and then in particular to the Yuba River, which is this wild river,
sentences.zh: 后来随着我们长大，香卡，我们开始做的事情是去河流漂流，特别是去尤巴河，那是一条狂野的河流，

sentences.en: And so I had this incredible childhood of biking and walking out in the country.
sentences.zh: 所以我拥有了一个在乡村骑车和漫步的不可思议的童年。

sentences.en: We lived on a dirt road where when I'd go walk home from the school dance, it was pitch black.
sentences.zh: 我们住在一条土路上，当我从学校舞会走回家时，外面漆黑一片。

sentences.en: And I'd see this giant sky of stars, shooting stars.
sentences.zh: 我会看到巨大的星空，还有流星。

sentences.en: So it was about wild awe.
sentences.zh: 所以那是一种关于狂野的敬畏。

sentences.en: So that brings me to a question that I've been pondering for a bit in this conversation, which is that awe in general seems like an ineffable emotion.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了我在这次谈话中一直在思考的一个问题，那就是敬畏通常看起来是一种难以言表的情绪。

sentences.en: It feels like it's very hard to wrap your arms around what exactly it is.
sentences.zh: 感觉很难确切地把握它到底是什么。

sentences.en: And if you're going to study it scientifically, you have to know what it is that you're studying.
sentences.zh: 如果你要科学地研究它，你必须知道你研究的到底是什么。

sentences.en: So about 20 years ago, I understand that you and a collaborator came up with a working definition of awe.
sentences.zh: 所以大约20年前，我了解到你和一位合作者提出了一个关于敬畏的工作定义。

sentences.en: Can you tell me how that came about?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我那是怎么来的吗？

sentences.en: It seems ineffable and beyond words, but yet people really want to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 它似乎难以言表，超出了语言的范畴，但人们却非常想谈论它。

sentences.en: It's mysterious and numinous, and we probably can measure it.
sentences.zh: 它神秘而神圣，我们或许可以测量它。

sentences.en: And that's one of the tasks of science.
sentences.zh: 而这正是科学的任务之一。

sentences.en: So Jonathan Haidt, who is an early collaborator in my career and brilliant mind, we got invited to write a paper for a special issue on pleasure.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·海特是我职业生涯早期的合作者，也是一位才华横溢的思想家，我们受邀为一期关于快乐的特刊撰写论文。

sentences.en: And John and I had been talking about awe, and we said awe, the key elements are when we encounter vast mysteries that we can't understand with our current knowledge.
sentences.zh: 约翰和我一直在谈论敬畏，我们说敬畏的关键要素在于，当我们遇到用现有知识无法理解的巨大奥秘时。

sentences.en: Or what we said was awe requires what we call the need for accommodation.
sentences.zh: 或者我们所说的是，敬畏需要我们所谓的“顺应需求”。

sentences.en: You have to rearrange your knowledge structures just to make sense of what you've encountered.
sentences.zh: 你必须重新调整你的知识结构，才能理解你所遇到的事物。

sentences.en: But I think for our conversation today, it's really awe is encountering vast mysteries that we don't understand.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于我们今天的谈话来说，敬畏其实就是遇到我们无法理解的巨大奥秘。

sentences.en: So nature is very often a common source of awe for many people.
sentences.zh: 所以大自然往往是许多人敬畏的共同来源。

sentences.en: I want to play for you an audio clip.
sentences.zh: 我想为你播放一段音频片段。

sentences.en: This is from a video made by a man named Paul Vasquez.
sentences.zh: 这是来自一个叫保罗·瓦斯奎兹的人制作的视频。

sentences.en: He saw something outside his home in Yosemite.
sentences.zh: 他在优胜美地的家外看到了某种景象。

sentences.en: Oh my god, oh my god, oh my god, oh my god, oh my god, oh my god, it's full on, double rainbow all the way across the sky, oh my god.
sentences.zh: 我的天哪，我的天哪，我的天哪，我的天哪，我的天哪，我的天哪，太壮观了，双彩虹横跨整个天空，我的天哪。

sentences.en: So, Dakar, you've seen this video, I believe.
sentences.zh: 所以，达克，我相信你见过这个视频。

sentences.en: As a scientist, would you care to hazard a guess at what's happening inside Paul Vasquez's mind at that moment?
sentences.zh: 作为一名科学家，你愿意试着猜测一下保罗·瓦斯奎兹在那一刻内心在想什么吗？

sentences.en: This video is really what mystical experiences are like for people.
sentences.zh: 这个视频真实地展现了人们所经历的神秘体验。

sentences.en: They laugh, they use language that is expansive and beyond the usual kinds of terms we use.
sentences.zh: 他们会大笑，使用那种宽广的、超出我们常用词汇的语言。

sentences.en: It's full on, it's oh my god.
We cry, we are moved outside of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们会哭泣，我们被带离了自我。

sentences.en: You know, I want to play you a clip from the end of the same video, Dakar,
sentences.zh: 你知道，达克，我想给你播放同一视频结尾的一段片段，

sentences.en: because it brings up something that I want to ask you about.
sentences.zh: 因为它引出了我想问你的事情。

sentences.en: Oh my god, what does it mean?
sentences.zh: 我的天哪，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: I don't know what it means.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这意味着什么。

sentences.en: You know, it's interesting, Paul is almost uncomfortable by the intensity of the experience.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很有趣，保罗几乎因为这种体验的强烈程度而感到不安。

sentences.en: He's struggling to understand what it means.
sentences.zh: 他在努力理解这意味着什么。

sentences.en: And I think when most people think about awe, they think about, okay, I'm seeing something beautiful, I see a beautiful sight.
sentences.zh: 我认为当大多数人想到敬畏时，他们会想，好吧，我看到了美丽的东西，我看到了美丽的景色。

sentences.en: But I think we're getting into deeper waters here where awe can actually make us uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们正在进入更深的水域，敬畏实际上会让我们感到不安。
是的，你知道，敬畏会让人失去平衡。

sentences.en: It introduces profound uncertainty about our understanding of the world.
sentences.zh: 它引入了关于我们对世界理解的深刻不确定性。

sentences.en: It can be filled with threat.
You know, when I sat amidst a storm, you know, I felt threatened.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我坐在风暴中时，你知道，我感到受到了威胁。

sentences.en: Just recently, I was backpacking with my daughter Natalie High Sierras, and we got caught in a lightning storm.
sentences.zh: 就在最近，我和女儿娜塔莉在高内华达山脉背包旅行，我们被困在了一场雷暴中。

sentences.en: And it was awe-inspiring and threatening, and that is true, I believe, with Vasquez's experience, the double rainbow experience.
sentences.zh: 那既令人敬畏又充满威胁，我相信瓦斯奎兹的双彩虹体验也是如此。

sentences.en: You know, when we no longer can make sense of reality, which is a theme of awe, it's that mystery, it's the need for finding new understandings of the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们不再能理解现实时，这就是敬畏的主题，那是奥秘，是需要为世界寻找新理解的需求。

sentences.en: Often, we feel adrift, we feel anxious, we feel threatened, and we feel destabilized.
sentences.zh: 通常，我们感到漂泊，感到焦虑，感到受威胁，感到失去平衡。

sentences.en: You found that another realm of experience that tends to inspire awe involves other people who do amazing things.
sentences.zh: 你发现另一种往往能激发敬畏的体验领域涉及那些做出惊人举动的人。

sentences.en: Tell me about the idea of moral beauty, Dakar.
sentences.zh: 跟我谈谈道德美的概念吧，达克。

sentences.en: You know, moral beauty is the idea that other people's kindness and courage and overcoming obstacles and their virtuosity and their discipline can inspire us morally,
sentences.zh: 你知道，道德美是指他人的善良、勇气、克服障碍以及他们的精湛技艺和自律可以激发我们的道德感，

sentences.en: where we see in them what we want to be as good human beings.
sentences.zh: 我们在他们身上看到了我们想要成为的好人的样子。

sentences.en: And it astonished us, Shankar, at the Berkeley Lab, that, you know, we sent out these requests, 26 countries, all these stories of awe come rolling in,
sentences.zh: 香卡，在伯克利实验室，我们感到惊讶的是，你知道，我们发出了这些请求，来自26个国家，所有关于敬畏的故事纷至沓来，

sentences.en: and the most universal and the most common was the goodness or moral beauty of other people right around them.
sentences.zh: 而最普遍、最常见的就是他们身边人的善良或道德美。

sentences.en: And I'm not talking about Mahatma Gandhi or Mother Teresa.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是圣雄甘地或特蕾莎修女。

sentences.en: It is like neighbors and strangers and grandmothers and the like and roommates that almost on a weekly basis are triggering us to feel like,
sentences.zh: 就像邻居、陌生人、祖母之类的人，还有室友，几乎每周都在触发我们产生这种感觉：

sentences.en: God, people are good, and I could be inspired by that.
sentences.zh: 天哪，人们真好，我能从中受到启发。

sentences.en: I understand that you once had a powerful experience with a spiritual leader that also inspired a feeling of awe.
sentences.zh: 我了解到你曾经与一位精神领袖有过一次强有力的经历，那也激发了一种敬畏感。

sentences.en: Tell me about your encounter with the Dalai Lama.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲你与达赖喇嘛的会面吧。

sentences.en: It makes me humble to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 谈论这件事让我感到谦卑。

sentences.en: You know, I've been on two panels with His Holiness the Dalai Lama, and I'm like, man, I'm on a stage with the Dalai Lama,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我和达赖喇嘛尊者一起参加过两次小组讨论，我当时想，天哪，我和达赖喇嘛同台了，

sentences.en: and there are 2,500 people out in the audience.
Before we go on, I greet His Holiness.
sentences.zh: 在我们上台之前，我向尊者致意。

sentences.en: When He looks you in the eye, man, you feel like He is really looking me in the eye.
sentences.zh: 当他看着你的眼睛时，伙计，你会觉得他真的在看着我的眼睛。

sentences.en: And we hugged, and He kind of tickled me.
sentences.zh: 我们拥抱了，他甚至还挠了我一下。

sentences.en: And I was, and I literally, I was one giant goose bump.
sentences.zh: 我当时，我真的，我全身都起了一层鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: You know, I was like, wow, I've just hugged and been tickled by the Dalai Lama.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时想，哇，我刚刚拥抱了达赖喇嘛，还被他挠了。

sentences.en: Then we go on stage, and, you know, and I'm asking him these dumb questions, and, you know, the neuroscientiSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我们上台，你知道，我问他那些愚蠢的问题，你知道，神经科学家。

sentences.en: And he's so engaged and interested and curious, you know, because he's training his mind in a way.
sentences.zh: 他非常投入、感兴趣且好奇，你知道，因为他正在以某种方式训练他的心智。

sentences.en: He's working harder on his mind than I've ever worked on anything.
sentences.zh: 他在心智上所下的功夫比我做任何事情都要多。

sentences.en: And at one moment in this conversation, I'm asking him about compassion, and he says, compassion is the natural state of the mind.
sentences.zh: 在这次谈话的某一刻，我问他关于慈悲的问题，他说，慈悲是心智的自然状态。

sentences.en: And I, you know, coming out of my Western scientific homo economicus mindset, I was just, it was an epiphany.
sentences.zh: 而我，你知道，带着我西方科学的“经济人”思维，我当时，那简直是一个顿悟。

sentences.en: And epiphanies are a very subtle source of awe where suddenly we grasp that there are big ideas that really make sense of a lot of things in reality.
sentences.zh: 顿悟是一种非常微妙的敬畏来源，突然间我们领悟到，有一些宏大的思想确实解释了现实中的许多事情。

sentences.en: You might find epiphanies in the idea of free markets or evolution or that capitalism is bad for the planet or big data or the idea of quantum physics, right?
sentences.zh: 你可能会在自由市场、进化论、资本主义对地球有害、大数据或量子物理学的概念中找到顿悟，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's surprisingly common around the world and has this structure to seeing suddenly being revealed to big ideas that help you make sense of the mysteries that concern you.
sentences.zh: 这在世界各地出奇地普遍，并且具有这种结构：突然揭示出那些能帮助你理解困扰你的奥秘的宏大思想。

sentences.en: And it was an awe moment, right?
sentences.zh: 那是一个敬畏的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: I was like, wait a minute.
Compassion is the deepest structure in the human mind down in the midbrain, all these structures that have been part of mammalian evolution.
sentences.zh: 慈悲是人类心智中最深层的结构，位于中脑，所有这些结构都是哺乳动物进化的一部分。

sentences.en: And that animated a lot of research I did on compassion and changed how I teach.
sentences.zh: 这激发了我所做的许多关于慈悲的研究，并改变了我的教学方式。

sentences.en: And it changed how I thought about humanity, you know, that there is this deep goodness in us that's part of our evolutionary story.
sentences.zh: 它改变了我对人类的看法，你知道，我们内心深处存在着这种善良，这是我们进化故事的一部分。

sentences.en: That's one of the most interesting parts of our evolutionary story, how good we are.
sentences.zh: 这是我们进化故事中最有趣的部分之一，我们是多么善良。

sentences.en: You know, you talked about going to see Iggy Pop and then feeling like you could go on stage, you know, and talk to 300 students with newfound confidence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你谈到去看伊基·波普的演出，然后感觉自己可以上台，你知道，带着新的自信去和300名学生交谈。

sentences.en: Did you find the same thing happened after meeting the Dalai Lama?
sentences.zh: 你发现见到达赖喇嘛后也发生了同样的情况吗？

sentences.en: Did your life feel different in the days and weeks that followed?
sentences.zh: 在接下来的日子和几周里，你的生活感觉有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: After that experience with His Holiness the Dalai Lama, I felt like I had a deeper sense of purpose and meaning.
sentences.zh: 在与达赖喇嘛尊者的那次经历之后，我觉得自己有了更深的目标感和意义感。

sentences.en: And so, you know, I'm on an airplane and I had profound flight anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我在飞机上，我曾经有严重的飞行焦虑。

sentences.en: Every little bump felt like the end of my life.
sentences.zh: 每一次小颠簸都感觉像是我的生命终结了。

sentences.en: I'd have images of losing my life and my children and so forth.
sentences.zh: 我会产生失去生命、失去孩子等等的画面。

sentences.en: And I noticed that I wasn't anxious on the flight.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我在飞行中不再焦虑了。

sentences.en: I didn't need to power down a whiskey to make it home, you know.
sentences.zh: 我不需要喝威士忌来让自己平静下来，你知道。

sentences.en: And then I got there and I was at the carousel and, of course, my luggage was loSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我到了那里，我在行李转盘旁，当然，我的行李丢了。

sentences.en: And I literally laughed it off.
sentences.zh: 我真的把它当作笑话一笑置之了。

sentences.en: And I think I said, good, you know, time to shed all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想我说，太好了，你知道，是时候摆脱所有这些东西了。

sentences.en: I truly felt, and this is true of the science of awe, which is the mundane things don't get to you as much.
sentences.zh: 我真的感觉到了，敬畏科学也是如此，即平凡的事情不会再那么影响你了。

sentences.en: And I felt above them and strong.
sentences.zh: 我感到超越了它们，并且很强大。

sentences.en: So, I think, you know, all of us have had these experiences where we have that warm glow we get from, you know, an encounter with an awe-inspiring person or an experience.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想，你知道，我们所有人都经历过这些时刻，我们从与一个令人敬畏的人或经历的相遇中获得了那种温暖的光芒。

sentences.en: Is there any risk, Thacker, that this can act, you know, like a kind of drug,
sentences.zh: 塔克，有没有一种风险，这可能会像一种毒品，

sentences.en: that we get a high from feeling awestruck and inspired and then this can lead us to be complacent or even oblivious to the sorrows or horrors of the world?
sentences.zh: 我们从感到敬畏和受启发中获得快感，然后这会导致我们变得自满，甚至对世界的悲伤或恐怖视而不见？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there are many risks of awe, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为敬畏有很多风险，对吧？
这是一种让人失去平衡的情绪。

sentences.en: It leads you to look for new knowledge to make sense of the world.
sentences.zh: 它引导你去寻找新的知识来理解世界。

sentences.en: It leads you to abandon past knowledge structures, perhaps, or assumptions.
sentences.zh: 它引导你放弃过去的知识结构，或者假设。

sentences.en: And, you know, a parent might think of, well, that's what happened to my daughter when she joined a cult.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，一位家长可能会想，嗯，我女儿加入邪教时就是这样。

sentences.en: As this cult leader suddenly persuaded her to abandon life and follow this new awe-inspiring figure.
sentences.zh: 当这个邪教领袖突然说服她放弃生活，追随这个新的令人敬畏的人物时。

sentences.en: You know, there's a new concern in the psychedelic movement of, for certain people who find too much, you know, destabilizing search for new meaning in psychedelic experiences,
sentences.zh: 你知道，迷幻药运动中有一个新的担忧，对于某些在迷幻体验中发现太多，你知道，对寻找新意义感到失去平衡的人来说，

sentences.en: it can get them into trouble.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让他们陷入麻烦。

sentences.en: Pierre Carlo Valdezolo has, you know, nice studies showing that certain kinds of awe make us see kind of patterns where there aren't patterns.
sentences.zh: 皮埃尔·卡洛·瓦尔德佐洛有一些很好的研究表明，某些类型的敬畏会让我们在没有模式的地方看到模式。

sentences.en: And so we can believe things, you know, maybe a QAnon supporter feels goosebumps and awe at these stories that are absolute nonsense.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可能会相信一些事情，你知道，也许一个“匿名者Q”的支持者在听到这些完全荒谬的故事时会感到起鸡皮疙瘩和敬畏。

sentences.en: They don't have a sense of boundaries.
So, yeah, there are risks here that we should be attentive to.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这里确实存在我们应该注意的风险。

sentences.en: As there are, Shankar, with every human passion.
sentences.zh: 正如香卡所说，每一种人类激情都存在风险。

sentences.en: So, you've become increasingly interested in the evolutionary origins of awe.
sentences.zh: 所以，你对敬畏的进化起源越来越感兴趣了。

sentences.en: Why is it that we would have an emotion like this?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会拥有这样一种情绪？

sentences.en: You know, it's possible that other species also experience awe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其他物种也可能体验到敬畏。

sentences.en: But, of course, you know, we don't typically see a line of cats sitting and watching the sunset together, right?
sentences.zh: 但当然，你知道，我们通常不会看到一排猫坐在一起看日落，对吧？

sentences.en: So, is there something that might explain our predisposition to awe from an evolutionary perspective?
sentences.zh: 那么，有没有什么东西可以从进化角度解释我们对敬畏的倾向？

sentences.en: You know, this is where the science of awe gets really interesting, which is how far back in our primate mammalian evolution can we trace this, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是敬畏科学变得非常有趣的地方，即我们可以追溯到我们灵长类哺乳动物进化的多远，对吧？

sentences.en: If it is a basic emotion, and we have a lot of data that suggests awe is as basic to humanity and the human species as anger or fear.
sentences.zh: 如果它是一种基本情绪，我们有大量数据表明，敬畏对人类和人类物种来说，就像愤怒或恐惧一样基本。

sentences.en: And we have a lot of data on the expression of awe and what it does to our social behavior and sense of self that awe is this pretty deep human universal emotion.
sentences.zh: 我们有大量关于敬畏的表达以及它对我们的社会行为和自我意识的影响的数据，表明敬畏是一种非常深刻的人类普遍情绪。

sentences.en: And I think that it does two things that are vital to our evolution.
sentences.zh: 我认为它做了两件对我们进化至关重要的事情。

sentences.en: And the first is it connects the individual to collectives.
sentences.zh: 第一点是它将个体与集体联系起来。

sentences.en: And time and time again, when people experience awe, they see things like,
sentences.zh: 一次又一次，当人们体验到敬畏时，他们会看到诸如……

sentences.en: I felt small, and I felt like I was part of something larger than myself.
sentences.zh: 我感到自己很渺小，也感到自己是比我自身更宏大事物的一部分。

sentences.en: And this is fundamental to our survival.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的生存至关重要。

sentences.en: And then the other thing that I think is really important, Shankar, is that awe helps us see the systems around us and understand them.
sentences.zh: 还有一点我认为非常重要，尚卡尔，那就是敬畏感能帮助我们观察并理解周围的系统。

sentences.en: One of the sets of operations of our mind is to be very narrow and focus on the self and individual actions and cause and effect relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们大脑运作的模式之一，是极其狭隘地专注于自我、个人行为以及因果关系。

sentences.en: The other is to look at the world holistically and systemically.
sentences.zh: 而另一种模式则是从整体和系统的角度去看待世界。
这是一个社会等级制度。

sentences.en: And awe pops those systems out to our awareness.
sentences.zh: 而敬畏感能让这些系统跃入我们的意识之中。

sentences.en: So it really is the animator of a systems view of life.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实是生命系统观的推动者。

sentences.en: And that's really important for scientific understanding, for social understanding, for knowing where to find resources in my environment, right, to understand my ecology.
sentences.zh: 这对科学认知、社会认知，以及了解如何在环境中寻找资源——也就是理解我的生态环境——都非常重要，对吧？

sentences.en: And awe is the great engine of a systems view of the world.
sentences.zh: 敬畏感是世界系统观的伟大引擎。

sentences.en: You know, and so much of it begins with the feeling that awe can produce in us of making us feel small.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一切很大程度上始于敬畏感在我们心中产生的那种让我们感到渺小的感觉。

sentences.en: I remember visiting Alaska once and feeling like I was a very small creature on a very, very big planet.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次去阿拉斯加，感觉自己就像是一个非常、非常大星球上的一个非常渺小的生物。

sentences.en: And you've done studies looking at the same idea.
sentences.zh: 你做过研究来探讨同样的观点。

sentences.en: You ran an interesting study in Yosemite exploring this idea that awe changes our sense of our own scale.
sentences.zh: 你在优胜美地进行了一项有趣的研究，探讨了敬畏感如何改变我们对自己尺度感的认知。

sentences.en: You know, the self takes up a lot of area in the brain and in our consciousness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自我意识在大脑和我们的意识中占据了很大的空间。

sentences.en: We're always thinking, especially in this modern world, about my goals, my status, my aspirations, what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 我们总是——尤其是在这个现代世界里——在思考我的目标、我的地位、我的抱负，以及我正在做的事情。
那是我的欲望，我的兴趣。

sentences.en: And evolutionists have really talked about the problem of self-intereSt.
sentences.zh: 进化论者确实讨论过利己主义的问题。

sentences.en: How do we get people to orient to other people, to societies and collectives?
sentences.zh: 我们如何让人们去关注他人、社会和集体？

sentences.en: And we started to have this idea that awe does that by creating the small self.
sentences.zh: 我们开始有了这样一个想法：敬畏感通过创造“渺小的自我”来做到这一点。

sentences.en: In a lot of writings about awe, right, religious writings from centuries ago, nature writings, Ralph Waldo Emerson, his big epiphany, I am nothing, right, psychedelic writings.
sentences.zh: 在许多关于敬畏的著作中，比如几个世纪前的宗教著作、自然文学、拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生的顿悟——“我什么都不是”——以及迷幻文学中，都是如此。

sentences.en: All these writings are speaking to this, but we had to get it empirically.
sentences.zh: 所有这些著作都在谈论这一点，但我们需要实证研究来证实它。

sentences.en: So my collaborator, Yang Bai from China, went to Yosemite, stopped travelers from 42 countries at this particular outlook on a road where you first get to see Yosemite Valley.
sentences.zh: 所以我的合作者，来自中国的白杨（音译），去了优胜美地，在通往优胜美地山谷的一条路上，拦住了来自42个国家的游客，那个位置是第一次能看到山谷的地方。

sentences.en: And El Capitan and the great granite slabs and this incredible valley that's just awe-inspiring.
sentences.zh: 那里有酋长岩、巨大的花岗岩板，还有那个令人惊叹、充满敬畏感的山谷。

sentences.en: And what Yang Bai did is she did a really simple task.
sentences.zh: 白杨做了一个非常简单的任务。

sentences.en: She had people at that moment draw themselves and write me.
sentences.zh: 她让人们在那一刻画出自己，并写下“我”。

sentences.en: And in that context, those drawings of the self were really small.
sentences.zh: 在这种情境下，那些关于自我的画作确实非常小。

sentences.en: They wrote their sense of me really small compared to the right kind of control conditions.
sentences.zh: 与对照组相比，他们写下的“我”的意识非常小。

sentences.en: And we have other data and really different kinds of data, even neuroscientific data showing awe quiets this egoistic,
sentences.zh: 我们还有其他数据，甚至是完全不同类型的神经科学数据，显示敬畏感能平息这种利己的、

sentences.en: self-focused sense of personal identity and opens you up to the big things that you're connected to.
sentences.zh: 以自我为中心的个人认同感，让你向与你相连的宏大事物敞开心扉。

sentences.en: You and your collaborator, Lani Shioda, also once had people stand in front of an enormous T-Rex skeleton.
sentences.zh: 你和你的合作者拉尼·希奥达也曾让人们站在一具巨大的霸王龙骨架前。

sentences.en: Tell me about that experiment, Dakar.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那个实验吧，达克尔。

sentences.en: On the Berkeley campus, we have this incredible replica of a T-Rex skeleton.
sentences.zh: 在伯克利校园里，我们有一个令人难以置信的霸王龙骨架复制品。

sentences.en: And it's in our Museum of Paleontology.
sentences.zh: 它就在我们的古生物学博物馆里。

sentences.en: And you stand next to it.
And we did the pilot testing.
People say, I feel awe, man.
sentences.zh: 人们说，伙计，我感到敬畏。

sentences.en: Imagine being chased by that thing, you know.
sentences.zh: 想象一下被那东西追赶，你知道的。

sentences.en: Wow, those things existed 70 million years ago?
sentences.zh: 哇，那些东西在7000万年前就存在了？

sentences.en: So Lani and our team stood Berkeley undergraduates by this T-Rex or they stood in the opposite direction looking down a hallway.
sentences.zh: 所以拉尼和我们的团队让伯克利的本科生站在霸王龙旁边，或者让他们站在相反的方向看着走廊。

sentences.en: And there's this classic measure of your own self or identity, which is you are given the stem, I am, and next to it is a blank line.
sentences.zh: 有一个经典的衡量自我或认同感的指标，就是给你一个词干“我是”，旁边是一条空白横线。

sentences.en: And you just fill it in 20 different times.
sentences.zh: 你只需要填上20个不同的内容。

sentences.en: And typically, people living in the West will say things like, I am, you know, extroverted, and I am ambitious, and I am interested in this.
sentences.zh: 通常，生活在西方的人会说，比如，“我是外向的”，“我是有野心的”，“我对这个感兴趣”。

sentences.en: And when they stood next to that T-Rex and took it in and felt awe, their sense of self expanded and themes of common humanity emerged.
sentences.zh: 而当他们站在那具霸王龙旁边，沉浸其中并感受到敬畏时，他们的自我感扩展了，共同人性的主题浮现了出来。

sentences.en: I am a part of California.
I am of this ethnic variety.
And so this collective communal self emerged.
sentences.zh: 于是，这种集体性的自我感就出现了。

sentences.en: And that's the power of awe.
A little moment, 30 seconds of it, you shift from self-focus, very narrow, to, wow, I'm part of something really large.
sentences.zh: 只需短短30秒，你就从狭隘的自我关注，转变为“哇，我是某个宏大事物的一部分”。

sentences.en: And some of this translates not just to how we think about ourselves in our own minds, but how we're acting towards other people.
sentences.zh: 这不仅转化为我们大脑中对自我的思考方式，也转化为我们对待他人的行为方式。

sentences.en: You also ran another experiment on the Berkeley campus, this time involving a grove of eucalyptus trees.
sentences.zh: 你还在伯克利校园做了另一个实验，这次涉及一片桉树林。

sentences.en: Tell me about that study, Ducker.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲那个研究吧，达克尔。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, one of the beauties of awe, and to understand it, it brings out the best of our imagination, you know.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，敬畏的美妙之处在于——要理解它——它能激发我们最好的想象力，你知道的。

sentences.en: And my lab started to get interested in awe, and we were throwing around all these ideas and doing these crazy studies.
sentences.zh: 我的实验室开始对敬畏产生兴趣，我们讨论了各种想法，并做了这些疯狂的研究。

sentences.en: And the very imaginative Paul Piff, now a professor at UC Irvine, did a study in which he took undergrads to a eucalyptus grove.
sentences.zh: 极具想象力的保罗·皮夫（现为加州大学尔湾分校教授）做了一项研究，他带本科生去了一片桉树林。

sentences.en: And they're blue gum eucalyptus trees.
They're some of the tallest in North America.
sentences.zh: 它们是北美最高的树木之一。

sentences.en: When you look up into them, their light and the colors and the leaves and their fragrances are just astonishing.
sentences.zh: 当你抬头仰望它们时，光线、色彩、叶子和芬芳简直令人惊叹。

sentences.en: That grove, when you stand in the middle of them, embraces you.
sentences.zh: 当你站在那片树林中间时，它拥抱着你。

sentences.en: It makes you feel like you're a part of them.
sentences.zh: 它让你感觉自己是它们的一部分。

sentences.en: And in the control condition, people were in the same place, but they looked at this science building.
sentences.zh: 在对照组中，人们在同一个地方，但他们看的是一栋科学大楼。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, you know, Shankar, this is a minute or two of just for no reason looking up into these trees.
sentences.zh: 结果你猜怎么着，尚卡尔，这只是无缘无故地抬头看了一两分钟的树。

sentences.en: In one to two minutes, our students reported feeling less narcissistic, less entitled.
sentences.zh: 在一两分钟内，我们的学生报告说感觉没那么自恋了，也没那么自以为是了。

sentences.en: They needed less money to do the study when we offered to pay them.
sentences.zh: 当我们提出付钱给他们时，他们对报酬的要求也降低了。

sentences.en: And then Paul staged this accident where a student was walking by, and they dropped some pens.
sentences.zh: 然后保罗安排了一场意外，一个学生走过时掉了一些笔。

sentences.en: And the people feeling awe picked up more pens, right?
sentences.zh: 而那些感受到敬畏的人捡起了更多的笔，对吧？

sentences.en: And we replicated that in tightly controlled laboratory studies.
sentences.zh: 我们在严格控制的实验室研究中重复了这一结果。

sentences.en: You just share more when you're feeling awe.
sentences.zh: 当你感受到敬畏时，你就是会分享更多。

sentences.en: Just with a minute or two of looking up at some trees.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为抬头看了几分钟树。

sentences.en: You know, very much like you described about your own experiences in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这和你描述的自己在威斯康星州的经历非常相似。

sentences.en: You and Jonathan Haidt have said that an experience of awe can press a reset button in the mind.
sentences.zh: 你和乔纳森·海特曾说，敬畏的体验可以按下大脑的重置按钮。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that, Dakar?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思，达克尔？

sentences.en: And actually, you know, Sylvan Tompkins wrote about when you're startled by a loud clap of thunder or the appearance of an old friend or bumping into a friend in the street.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，西尔万·汤姆金斯曾写道，当你被一声响亮的雷声吓到，或者看到一位老朋友，或者在街上偶遇朋友时，

sentences.en: It kind of restarts your mind.
It resets it to look at things anew and fresh.
sentences.zh: 它将其重置，让你以全新的视角看待事物。

sentences.en: And contemplative people might say, with a beginner's mind.
sentences.zh: 修行者可能会说，这是以“初学者的心态”。

sentences.en: And that's what awe does for us, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 这就是敬畏为我们所做的，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to bring more awe into our lives.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨如何让生活中充满更多敬畏感。
你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: At UC Berkeley, psychologist Dakar Keltner studies the benevolent emotions, including the emotion of awe.
sentences.zh: 在加州大学伯克利分校，心理学家达克尔·凯尔特纳研究仁慈的情绪，包括敬畏感。

sentences.en: He's the author of the book, Awe, The New Science of Everyday Wonder and How It Can Transform Your Life.
sentences.zh: 他是《敬畏：日常奇迹的新科学及其如何改变你的人生》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Dakar, you recently studied the effects of awe on disadvantaged students and military veterans.
sentences.zh: 达克尔，你最近研究了敬畏感对弱势学生和退伍军人的影响。

sentences.en: Neither felt much awe in their regular lives.
sentences.zh: 他们平时生活中都没怎么感受到敬畏。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, there's a growing interest in our culture and scientifically about how the institutional structural traumas of life,
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我们的文化和科学界对生活中的制度性创伤越来越感兴趣，

sentences.en: if you're impoverished and you don't have parks nearby and the like, or you have a career like veterans who go see combat and see people die, their profiles look traumatized.
sentences.zh: 如果你很贫困，附近没有公园之类的设施，或者像退伍军人那样经历过战斗、目睹过死亡，他们的心理状况看起来就像是受过创伤。

sentences.en: They are depressed and vigilant, anxious very often, twice the rates of American citizens, elevated levels of cortisol and inflammation and the like.
sentences.zh: 他们经常感到抑郁、警觉、焦虑，比例是普通美国公民的两倍，皮质醇和炎症水平也较高。

sentences.en: And I became friends with Stacy Bear, who's a veteran, and we started talking about this.
sentences.zh: 我和一位退伍军人斯泰西·贝尔成了朋友，我们开始讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: And he leads veterans into outdoors prograMs.
sentences.zh: 他带领退伍军人参加户外项目。

sentences.en: And so what we decided to do in this study is we got veterans and high school students who were in really tough, impoverished schools in parts of the East Bay in California.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定在这项研究中，找来退伍军人和加州东湾地区一些非常艰苦、贫困学校的高中生。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, where there are bars and police cars and no gardens, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 那里到处是酒吧、警车，没有花园等等。

sentences.en: And these kids hadn't, you know, been outside in parks.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子以前没去过公园。

sentences.en: Many of them had not really seen a night sky of stars.
sentences.zh: 他们中许多人甚至没见过满天繁星的夜空。
所以我们带他们去漂流。

sentences.en: Our veterans and then our high schoolers down the American River on a stretch.
sentences.zh: 我们的退伍军人和高中生在美洲河的一段河道上漂流。

sentences.en: And you wind through these rapids and you look at the water and you see fish.
sentences.zh: 你穿过急流，看着水面，还能看到鱼。

sentences.en: And what we found, we measured their emotions and stress and trauma and sense of connection at the start of the study, a week later.
sentences.zh: 我们测量了他们在研究开始时以及一周后的情绪、压力、创伤和连接感。

sentences.en: And as the study unfolded, we measured their sense of wonder and awe and connection to their peers and cortisol and emotions.
sentences.zh: 随着研究的展开，我们测量了他们的惊奇感、敬畏感、与同伴的连接感、皮质醇水平和情绪。

sentences.en: And what we found is our high schoolers a week later felt less stress, more happiness.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，一周后，我们的高中生感到压力减轻了，幸福感增加了。

sentences.en: They felt more connected to their community and family.
sentences.zh: 他们感到与社区和家庭的联系更紧密了。

sentences.en: And our veterans felt 30 percent less PTSD.
sentences.zh: 而我们的退伍军人的创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）症状减轻了30%。

sentences.en: One high schooler said, I'm so struck by the rolling hills and the smoke.
sentences.zh: 一位高中生说，连绵的群山和烟雾让我深受震撼。

sentences.en: And it was smoky at the time because of wildfires and the water.
sentences.zh: 当时因为野火，空气中弥漫着烟雾，还有水面。

sentences.en: And then a veteran said, and I love this quote where, you know, the star splatted sky made me realize that my worries are not as important as I thought they are.
sentences.zh: 然后一位退伍军人说——我很喜欢这句话——“星光点点的天空让我意识到，我的烦恼并没有我想象的那么重要”。

sentences.en: But what I could do in the world is more important.
sentences.zh: “但我能为这个世界做的事情却更重要”。

sentences.en: And so it was this nice study.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项很棒的研究。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of science on this of different varieties that nature immersion and finding awe, gardening, walking, getting out into the woods,
sentences.zh: 关于这一点有各种各样的科学研究，即沉浸在自然中寻找敬畏感，比如园艺、散步、走进森林、

sentences.en: standing near a tree is good for your nervous system and your mind.
sentences.zh: 站在树旁，这对你的神经系统和大脑都有好处。

sentences.en: Is there any evidence that awe has physiological effects on us?
sentences.zh: 有证据表明敬畏感对我们有生理影响吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, there are, you know, there's this thing called the vagus nerve, largest bundle of nerves in your body.
sentences.zh: 有的，你知道，有一种东西叫迷走神经，它是你体内最大的神经束。

sentences.en: It slows heart rate, deepens breathing, regulates digestion, helps with your gut and the microbiome.
sentences.zh: 它能减缓心率、加深呼吸、调节消化，并有助于肠道和微生物群。

sentences.en: In general, people who have a nice functioning vagus nerve that is responsive and has elevated levels do better in life.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，迷走神经功能良好、反应灵敏且水平较高的人，生活得更好。

sentences.en: And we found, thanks to Amy Gordon and Jenny Stellar, you know, that little brief experiences of awe, seeing an inspiring image, hearing about moral beauty,
sentences.zh: 多亏了艾米·戈登和珍妮·斯特拉，我们发现，短暂的敬畏体验，比如看到鼓舞人心的图像、听到道德之美，
能提升你的迷走神经激活水平。

sentences.en: And then just as impressively, you know, when your immune system, the cytokine system more specifically, cranks out these proteins that attack pathogens,
sentences.zh: 同样令人印象深刻的是，当你的免疫系统——更具体地说是细胞因子系统——产生这些攻击病原体的蛋白质时，

sentences.en: and that's the inflammation response that makes you feel feverish and sluggish and overheated.
sentences.zh: 这就是导致你发烧、迟钝和过热的炎症反应。

sentences.en: It's good when you feel feverish, it's good when you feel feverish, it's good when you're fighting a virus, it's not good if you're chronically inflamed.
sentences.zh: 当你发烧时是好事，当你对抗病毒时是好事，但如果你长期处于炎症状态就不好了。

sentences.en: And it's one of the central threats to health in the United States.
sentences.zh: 这是美国健康面临的核心威胁之一。

sentences.en: And Jenny Stellar and Neha John Henderson went out and found in our lab that feeling a lot of awe of all the positive emotions quiets down the inflammation response.
sentences.zh: 珍妮·斯特拉和内哈·约翰·亨德森在我们的实验室发现，在所有积极情绪中，感受到强烈的敬畏感能平息炎症反应。

sentences.en: So it tells us, you know, Emerson, when he had this big epiphany of awe out on a cold day in Massachusetts, he said, there is nothing that nature cannot repair.
sentences.zh: 所以这告诉我们，爱默生在马萨诸塞州一个寒冷的日子里产生这种敬畏的顿悟时曾说，没有什么东西是自然无法修复的。

sentences.en: And I think he was feeling these changes in the body of vagal tone and inflammation, reduced inflammation, that awe gives us.
sentences.zh: 我认为他当时感受到的正是身体中迷走神经张力和炎症水平的变化，敬畏感减轻了炎症。

sentences.en: So, Dacher, you've described many ways in which awe is good for us, but you've also said that our society is becoming awe-deprived.
sentences.zh: 那么，达克尔，你描述了许多敬畏感对我们有益的方式，但你也说过我们的社会正变得“敬畏匮乏”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
The deeper structural conditions of our lives are, in some ways, especially for young people today, working against awe.
sentences.zh: 我们生活的深层结构条件，在某些方面，尤其是对今天的年轻人来说，正在阻碍敬畏感的产生。

sentences.en: And I really sense this teaching thousands of students a year at a big university like Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 在伯克利这样的大型大学里，每年教导成千上万的学生，我对此深有感触。

sentences.en: They are awe-deprived because too much is structured and they are not allowed to wander, like I did as a kid, wandering around the neighborhoods and out in the foothills.
sentences.zh: 他们处于“敬畏匮乏”状态，因为一切都结构化得太死板了，他们不被允许像我小时候那样，在社区和山脚下四处漫游。

sentences.en: They are awe-deprived because of the new technologies, which, frankly, just get us too focused on the self.
sentences.zh: 他们因为新技术而处于“敬畏匮乏”状态，坦率地说，这些技术让我们太专注于自我了。

sentences.en: The more we're focused on the self, the narrow parts of the self, the less awe we feel.
sentences.zh: 我们越专注于自我，越专注于自我的狭隘部分，我们感受到的敬畏就越少。

sentences.en: They're awe-deprived because of all the competitive self-comparisons that have arisen today.
sentences.zh: 他们因为当今社会出现的各种竞争性的自我比较而处于“敬畏匮乏”状态。

sentences.en: So, are people getting enough of it?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们得到足够的敬畏感了吗？

sentences.en: We need more awe right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在需要更多的敬畏感。

sentences.en: You know, Lancet publication recently showed that the pandemic has led to rises in depression and anxiety by 20 to 30 percent.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最近《柳叶刀》发表的一项研究显示，疫情导致抑郁和焦虑症的发病率上升了20%到30%。

sentences.en: We've all felt this, our young people in particular.
sentences.zh: 我们都感受到了这一点，尤其是我们的年轻人。
但生活中处处都有敬畏感。

sentences.en: And if we just take a little moment to get out and look for it, it's there to find.
sentences.zh: 如果我们花点时间走出去寻找，它就在那里等着我们发现。

sentences.en: So, Dacher, in one recent study, you had volunteers take an awe walk.
sentences.zh: 那么，达彻，在最近的一项研究中，你让志愿者们进行了一次“敬畏漫步”。

sentences.en: One of the easiest ways to find awe is to, in an unbounded way, go out and walk.
sentences.zh: 寻找敬畏感最简单的方法之一，就是以一种不受束缚的方式走出去散步。

sentences.en: We have been doing this as humans for a long time in the spiritual contemplative traditions.
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们在精神沉思的传统中已经这样做很久了。

sentences.en: Getting out into nature and doing awe walks is just part of those traditions.
sentences.zh: 走进大自然进行敬畏漫步，正是这些传统的一部分。

sentences.en: And what we decided to do is test its benefits scientifically.
sentences.zh: 我们决定通过科学的方法来验证它的益处。

sentences.en: And so, I wrote up these instructions for an awe walk.
sentences.zh: 于是，我为“敬畏漫步”写下了这些指导说明。

sentences.en: And what you do is you take your ordinary walk that a lot of people do.
sentences.zh: 你所要做的，就是像许多人那样进行一次普通的散步。

sentences.en: And, in fact, during the pandemic, there were historic levels of walking.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在疫情期间，人们的步行量达到了历史最高水平。

sentences.en: And you not only go out to do it vigorously and to help your heart, but you go with a childlike sense of wonder.
sentences.zh: 你不仅是为了锻炼身体、强健心脏而走，还要带着一种孩童般的惊奇感去走。

sentences.en: And you just stop and reflect on what is really interesting in the small things around you, the flowers and patterns of shadows and the like.
sentences.zh: 你要停下来，思考周围那些真正有趣的小事物，比如花朵、影子的图案等等。

sentences.en: And also look up, pass the horizon and look up to the vast things, right?
sentences.zh: 还要抬头看，越过地平线，去仰望那些宏大的事物，对吧？

sentences.en: And do it in a way where you go places that you're curious about.
sentences.zh: 而且要以一种去往你感到好奇的地方的方式去走。

sentences.en: And in this study, what we did is our participants were all 75 years old or older.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，我们的参与者年龄都在75岁或以上。

sentences.en: That is an age where, because we have a sense that death is coming and we see people die, we're a little bit more anxious at that stage of life.
sentences.zh: 在这个年纪，因为我们意识到死亡即将来临，也目睹过他人的离世，所以在这个人生阶段会感到更加焦虑。

sentences.en: And so, one group of our participants did an awe walk once a week for eight weeks.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的一组参与者每周进行一次敬畏漫步，持续八周。

sentences.en: The other group of participants, tight control, did a vigorous walk once a week.
sentences.zh: 另一组参与者作为严格对照组，每周进行一次剧烈运动式的步行。

sentences.en: Each time they did a walk, they took a picture of themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们每次散步时，都会给自己拍一张照片。

sentences.en: And then we gathered a bunch of self-reports, like how are they doing on a daily basis?
sentences.zh: 然后我们收集了大量自我报告，比如他们每天的状态如何？

sentences.en: How is their levels of anxiety and so forth?
sentences.zh: 他们的焦虑水平如何等等？

sentences.en: And we found just a couple of things.
One, the more you do the awe walk, the more awe-inspiring it becomes.
sentences.zh: 第一，敬畏漫步做得越多，它就越能激发敬畏感。
敬畏感并不会随着经验的增加而减弱。
它反而会变得更加丰富和深厚。

sentences.en: By the end of the eight weeks, our awe walk participants were feeling a lot of awe.
sentences.zh: 八周结束时，我们进行敬畏漫步的参与者感受到了强烈的敬畏感。

sentences.en: Two, more changes in the self.
sentences.zh: 第二，自我意识发生了更多变化。

sentences.en: The self gets smaller over time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，自我变得更小了。

sentences.en: And it starts to drift off to the side and they're including, you know, the rocks and sunsets of their awe walk.
sentences.zh: 它开始退居一旁，他们开始将敬畏漫步中看到的岩石、落日等事物纳入自我之中。

sentences.en: And then third, really importantly, on a daily basis, they just felt less distress.
sentences.zh: 第三，非常重要的一点是，在日常生活中，他们感受到的痛苦减少了。

sentences.en: You know, they felt less anxiety about life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们对生活的焦虑感减轻了。

sentences.en: You know, in many ways in this conversation, Dakar, we've spent a lot of time talking about awe in the beautiful and the majestic.
sentences.zh: 达彻，在这次谈话中，我们花了很多时间讨论关于美和宏大事物的敬畏感。

sentences.en: But you've written that so much of life is awesome, including the parts that are not great.
sentences.zh: 但你写过，生活中的许多事物都令人敬畏，包括那些并不美好的部分。

sentences.en: Tell me about your relationship with your brother, Rolf.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊你和你哥哥罗尔夫的关系吧。

sentences.en: You were very close to him, right?
sentences.zh: 你们以前非常亲密，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, just hearing you say his name brings goosebumps and tears to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，听到你叫他的名字，我都会起鸡皮疙瘩，热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: He was born one year after me, so he was younger.
sentences.zh: 他比我小一岁，所以他是弟弟。

sentences.en: We played basketball teams together, wandered together, went to Mexico together, were best men in each other's weddings.
sentences.zh: 我们一起参加篮球队，一起漫游，一起去墨西哥，还在彼此的婚礼上担任伴郎。

sentences.en: We both became social science-y teacher types.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都成了社会科学类的教师。

sentences.en: And frankly, he taught me how to be kinder and how to be courageous.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，是他教会了我如何变得更善良，如何变得勇敢。

sentences.en: I don't think I was endowed with those tendencies early.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我早年就具备这些天性。

sentences.en: He was my example in many ways of moral beauty.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，他都是我道德美的榜样。

sentences.en: So I was profoundly close to him through the ebbs and flows of brotherhood.
sentences.zh: 所以，在兄弟情谊的起起伏伏中，我与他有着深厚的感情。

sentences.en: So I understand a few years ago he was diagnosed with colon cancer.
sentences.zh: 我了解到几年前他被诊断出患有结肠癌。
跟我说说那段经历吧，达彻。

sentences.en: Anyone out listening, you know, who's been close to colon cancer, it's a horror show.
sentences.zh: 任何听众，如果曾与结肠癌近距离接触过，就会知道那是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: And for my brother, for two years I watched him, you know, go from being a 210-pound, very strong man, 147 pounds, bone thin, passing out.
sentences.zh: 对于我哥哥，我看着他整整两年，从一个210磅、非常强壮的男人，变成了147磅、瘦骨嶙峋、昏迷不醒的样子。

sentences.en: There's a lot of pain, but there are certain kinds of pain that just wipe out consciousness, break through pain.
sentences.zh: 有很多种痛苦，但有些痛苦会直接摧毁意识，突破忍受极限。

sentences.en: And abdominal pain is like that.
You know, chemotherapy, and I was just there all the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，化疗，我一直陪在他身边。

sentences.en: And then he decided to take a cocktail when he knew the cancer had returned and headed into his gut.
sentences.zh: 后来当他知道癌症复发并扩散到肠道时，他决定采取姑息治疗。

sentences.en: And we all went up there in January, and we watched him, you know, slowly leave this world.
sentences.zh: 一月份我们都赶了过去，看着他慢慢地离开这个世界。

sentences.en: And Shankar, I had gone through the most horrifying two years of my life, watching my companion in awe, my brother Rolf, fade physically.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我经历了人生中最可怕的两年，看着我的敬畏伙伴，我的哥哥罗尔夫，身体一点点衰竭。

sentences.en: But in that moment of seeing him calmer, heading into where he was going after losing his body, we were all around him, we touched him, the light felt different, we were quiet,
sentences.zh: 但在那一刻，看到他平静下来，在失去肉体后走向他要去的地方，我们都围在他身边，触摸着他，光线感觉不同了，我们很安静，

sentences.en: we bowed our heads, and we were all in reverence of my brother Rolf and what he meant.
sentences.zh: 我们低下了头，我们都在敬畏我的哥哥罗尔夫以及他所代表的一切。

sentences.en: And watching him go, I was filled with astonishment and awe.
sentences.zh: 看着他离去，我心中充满了惊奇和敬畏。

sentences.en: I understand that you took a trip to honor your brother's memory after he died.
sentences.zh: 我听说在他去世后，你进行了一次旅行来纪念他。

sentences.en: After he died, and then I returned to my life in Berkeley and was blown off the map.
sentences.zh: 他去世后，我回到伯克利继续生活，却感觉彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: And it's really the state that Joan Didion describes, you know, in her writing about grief.
sentences.zh: 那确实是琼·狄迪恩在描写悲伤时所描述的那种状态。

sentences.en: I couldn't sleep and anxious and confused and was just really struggling.
sentences.zh: 我无法入睡，焦虑不安，感到困惑，真的非常挣扎。

sentences.en: And this voice came to me, and it was, find awe.
sentences.zh: 这时一个声音出现在我脑海里，那就是：去寻找敬畏。

sentences.en: And my brother and I, we always went to the mountains.
sentences.zh: 我和我哥哥总是去山里。

sentences.en: You know, we grew up in the mountains near the Sierras, and I went up into the high Sierras and Ducks Lake where he and I had hiked, and Mammoth in the east side of the Sierras.
sentences.zh: 我们在内华达山脉附近的山区长大，我去了高地内华达山脉和鸭湖，那是我们曾经徒步过的地方，还有内华达山脉东侧的猛犸湖。

sentences.en: When I saw the ridgeline that he and I had seen, I felt him there.
sentences.zh: 当我看到我们曾经看过的山脊线时，我感觉他在那里。

sentences.en: I saw the trees that he and I had seen.
sentences.zh: 我看到了我们曾经见过的树木。

sentences.en: These trees flicker in the wind, the aspen trees.
sentences.zh: 那些在风中摇曳的树，白杨树。

sentences.en: And I just felt him there, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 我感觉他就在那里，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: I was like, in these mountains, my brother is with me.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，在这些山里，我哥哥和我在一起。

sentences.en: Dakar Keltner is a psychologist at the University of California, Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 达彻·凯尔特纳是加州大学伯克利分校的心理学家。

sentences.en: He's the author of Awe, the new science of everyday wonder and how it can transform your life.
sentences.zh: 他是《敬畏：日常惊奇的新科学及其如何改变你的生活》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Dakar, thank you for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 达彻，感谢你今天参加《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Shankar, it is a privilege to be in conversation with you.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，能与你交谈是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: When we come back, your questions answered.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将回答你的问题。

sentences.en: Mary Helen Immordino Yang responds to listeners' thoughts and stories about learning and what she calls transcendent thinking.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·海伦·伊莫迪诺-杨将回应听众关于学习以及她所称的“超越性思维”的想法和故事。
你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: There's more than one way to learn how to read and write.
sentences.zh: 学习读写的方法不止一种。

sentences.en: But if you grow up in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是在20世纪50年代的美国长大，

sentences.en: in the 1950s, your classes may have unfolded something like this.
sentences.zh: 你的课堂可能就是这样展开的。

sentences.en: As part of the reading readiness program, children are trained to look from left to right.
sentences.zh: 作为阅读准备课程的一部分，孩子们被训练从左向右看。

sentences.en: This is from a documentary released in 1956.
sentences.zh: 这段视频来自1956年发布的一部纪录片。

sentences.en: Children are sitting in rows of desks.
sentences.zh: 孩子们坐在成排的课桌前。

sentences.en: They are staring up at their teacher.
She walks them through reading and writing techniques.
sentences.zh: 老师引导他们学习读写技巧。

sentences.en: Phonics and the alphabet help children learn to spell.
sentences.zh: 自然拼读法和字母表帮助孩子们学习拼写。

sentences.en: Patty is arranging words in alphabetical order.
sentences.zh: 帕蒂正在按字母顺序排列单词。

sentences.en: Danny is dividing them into syllables.
sentences.zh: 丹尼正在把它们分成音节。

sentences.en: Kenneth is placing the accent marks.
sentences.zh: 肯尼斯正在放置重音符号。

sentences.en: Knowledge flows in one direction, from teacher to students.
sentences.zh: 知识单向流动，从老师流向学生。

sentences.en: There's an emphasis on rules and memorization.
sentences.zh: 重点在于规则和死记硬背。

sentences.en: Deanna and Wilder know they must practice, just as their parents and grandparents did,
sentences.zh: 迪安娜和怀尔德知道他们必须练习，就像他们的父母和祖父母一样，

sentences.en: This kind of teaching was the standard for a long time, in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这种教学方式在美国和其他地方长期以来都是标准，
并且在今天许多教室里依然存在。

sentences.en: and continues in many classrooms today.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，许多教育工作者和学校采用了替代性的学习方法。

sentences.en: But in more recent years, many educators and schools have embraced alternative approaches to learning.
sentences.zh: 体验式学习、基于问题的学习、基于项目的学习、

sentences.en: Experiential learning, problem-based learning, project-based learning,

sentences.zh: 所有这些方法都试图颠覆传统的教学模式。

sentences.en: All of these approaches attempt to upend the traditional model of teaching.
sentences.zh: 在南加州大学，心理学家和神经科学家玛丽·海伦·伊莫迪诺-杨

sentences.en: At the University of Southern California, psychologist and neuroscientist Mary Helen Imordino-Yang
sentences.zh: 认为任何教育方法都不应从所教的材料开始。

sentences.en: says any educational approach should start not with the material being taught.
It should start with the student.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·海伦是《隐藏的大脑》近期一期节目《我们的大脑如何学习》的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Mary Helen was a guest on a recent episode of Hidden Brain, titled How Our Brains Learn.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们请她回到节目中，回答你们关于学习科学的问题。

sentences.en: Today, we bring her back on the show to answer your questions about the science of learning.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·海伦·伊莫迪诺-杨，欢迎回到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Mary Helen Imordino-Yang, welcome back to Hidden Brain.
Thank you for having me back.
sentences.zh: 玛丽·海伦，我想从我们收到的一位名叫拉希德的听众的留言开始。

sentences.en: Mary Helen, I'd like to start with a message we received from a listener named Rashid.
sentences.zh: 这与他的一次学习经历有关，那次经历让他产生了各种负面的共鸣。

sentences.en: It had to do with a learning experience that resonated with him for all the wrong reasons.
sentences.zh: 六年级时，我妈妈给我报了游泳课，因为我不会游泳。

sentences.zh: 但她没有简单地传达数学概念，而是帮助他们看到这些数学概念
